description: focusing on building an end-to-end AI and computer vision pipeline using NASA open satellite data to address the challenge.
summary:
Ho Chi Minh City faces an ongoing urban land subsidence crisis. In low-lying southern and western districts like District 7, Nha Be, and Binh Tan, the ground sinks between 15 and 45 mm per year, mainly due to soft clay soils and heavy industrial groundwater extraction. Because of frequent monsoon cloud cover in southern Vietnam, optical satellites like Sentinel-2 or Landsat cannot clearly observe the surface for much of the year.

Our project, InSAR-SinkWatch, uses radar data based on the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission to track this movement. Using L-band radar (24 cm wavelength), the signal penetrates clouds and vegetation to measure surface elevation changes in millimeters. We built an interactive Python dashboard that displays subsidence rates, highlights areas sinking faster than 20 mm/year, and evaluates differential settlement risks to critical civil infrastructure like Metro Line 1.
details:
### 1. What does it do and how does it work?

InSAR-SinkWatch processes repeat-pass radar images to measure vertical ground motion across Ho Chi Minh City:

- Data Ingestion: It takes paired SAR acquisitions calibrated to NISAR L-band specifications (wavelength of 24.24 cm).

- Phase Processing: It calculates the interferometric phase difference between two repeat passes and applies an adaptive Goldstein phase filter to reduce decorrelation noise while preserving structural edges.

- Displacement Calculation: It converts the unwrapped phase into vertical surface displacement in millimeters using the physical formula: Delta_d = (wavelength / 4*pi) * Delta_phi.

- Hotspot Detection: An automated spatial routine identifies critical subsidence bowls where ground sinking exceeds 20 mm per year.

- Interactive Map & Risk Screening: Results are rendered on an interactive 3D Web GIS dashboard where users can explore sinking areas, assess differential settlement along Metro Line 1, and export standard GeoJSON files for QGIS and ArcGIS.

### 2. What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

- Works in All Weather: Radar waves penetrate rain, haze, and monsoon clouds, which are common in southern Vietnam and frequently blind optical satellites.

- Broad Urban Coverage: Unlike leveling benchmarks that only measure sparse fixed points, satellite radar maps millimeter ground motion across entire city districts simultaneously.

- Actionable Urban Planning: By identifying which municipal zones are subsiding fastest, city engineers can enforce groundwater pumping restrictions, reinforce flood barriers, and protect railway foundations against derailment risks.

### 3. What tools, coding languages, or software did you use?

- Python 3 as the core programming language.

- NumPy and SciPy for numerical matrix computing and 2D Fourier phase filtering algorithms.

- Streamlit and PyDeck (Deck.GL WebGL engine) for the interactive 3D Web GIS mission console.

- Matplotlib for scientific data visualization.

- GeoJSON standard format for vector interoperability with QGIS and ArcGIS.

### 4. How is your project creative?

Instead of generating static 2D maps or abstract tables of numbers, we combined radar interferometry with an interactive 3D Web GIS dashboard. Urban planners can adjust filter parameters, inspect interferogram phase fringes, view 3D downward-extruding ground depression bowls in real time, and simulate soil compaction forward to 2036.

### 5. What factors did your team consider?

Our team consists of two students—one in computer science and one in geography. We focused on the actual geotechnical and hydrological conditions of Ho Chi Minh City:

- The presence of 15 to 30-meter thick soft Holocene alluvial clay layers in southern districts (District 7, Nha Be) that compress easily under surface loads.

- The severe pore-water pressure drop caused by deep industrial groundwater extraction.

- How land subsidence worsens sunny-day tidal inundation along the Saigon and Dong Nai river corridors.
